Current position: do not approve the dashboard yet. It may make a change visible while leaving interpretation, authority, and exception handling exactly as ambiguous as before—only more official-looking.

The first thing I notice is that “the plan changed” has no defined source, recipient, or next-action owner. I would protect uncertainty about which failure matters, and whether the informal workarounds contain useful judgment that formalization would erase.

Hypotheses: changes are missed; changes are seen but understood differently; the response depends on context; or everyone waits because ownership is unclear. These need separate tests.

Questions: Who first knows? Who is affected? What happens when accounts conflict or the responsible person is unavailable? How is recovery recognized?

Recommended move: trace three recent changes end to end with the people involved, then run a one-week manual change log and explicit acknowledgment/owner handoff. Measure missed notices, interpretation disputes, stalled actions, and exception work. That experiment is reversible and will tell us whether any dashboard deserves to exist.
